title: Exome sequencing identifies ATP4A gene as responsible of an atypical familial type I gastric neuroendocrine tumour
authors: Calvete O, Reyes J, Zuñiga S, Paumard-Hernández B, Fernández V, Bujanda L, et al.
population: Consanguineous family with 10 children, 5 affected by type I gastric neuroendocrine tumour; sporadic gastric neuroendocrine tumour patients as comparison
funder: Not read: the publisher page shows the abstract only and the article is not in PubMed Central.
result: A homozygous ATP4A missense mutation (c.2107C>T, p.Arg703Cys) in a transmembrane domain prevents proton release by the parietal-cell pump and caused achlorhydria. Five of 10 siblings developed type I gastric neuroendocrine tumours from about 30 years of age, three with nodal infiltration requiring total gastrectomy and one with adenocarcinoma, with iron-deficiency rather than megaloblastic anaemia. No ATP4A mutations were found in sporadic gastric neuroendocrine tumours.
